enum.name: IHM_ENCODER_DIRECTION
enum.description: Rotary encoder movement direction. Mirrors RotaryEncoder.h's DIRECTION_TYPE exactly (IHM/lib/RotaryEncoder/RotaryEncoder.h) -- keep these two in sync if that enum ever changes.

entry.name: IHM_ENCODER_NOT_SUPPORTED
entry.description: No movement since this encoder was last read (RotaryEncoder:: getDirection() resets to this value after every read, so this also just means "nothing new since the last sample").

enum.name: PWM_FREQUENCY
enum.description: PWM channel frequency selector. Mirrors PWMFrequency in IHM/lib/MultiOutput/src/PWMTiming.h exactly (same order, same 0-based values) -- keep the two in sync if that enum ever changes. The trailing NUMBER_OF_PWM_FREQUENCIES count in the C enum is deliberately not mirrored here (it's a bound, not a value). Entry names carry the truncated integer Hz; the C enum's own names carry the exact fractional Hz.

entry.name: PWM_FREQUENCY_VARIABLE
entry.description: frequency_variable -- Fast PWM mode 14, TOP = ICRn. The PWM_CHANNEL_CONFIG.frequency field supplies that raw TOP; it is ignored for every other selector.

message.name: IHM_BOARD_STATE
message.description:
Periodic/on-change snapshot of the board's user-input state, analog inputs, and loop-timing debug info. Board -> PC, telemetry.
Field widths are intentionally not bit-packed across byte boundaries (e.g. each encoder gets its own byte rather than 3 encoders sharing 9 bits): with MAVLINK_MAX_PAYLOAD_LEN raised to 64 for future headroom, the few bytes saved by tight packing weren't worth the hand-rolled bit-shift/mask code on both the firmware and PC sides. This message is 19 bytes either way, well under the cap.
message.field: Bitmask of the 7 push-buttons, 1 = pressed. Bits 0-3: btn0-btn3. Bits 4-6: encoder0/1/2 push-buttons. Bit 7 unused (BinaryInput's own buildButtonMap() hardcodes this bit as a sentinel; we don't carry that here, it's just left 0).
Encoder 0 movement since last sample.
Encoder 1 movement since last sample.
Encoder 2 movement since last sample.
House-keeping orientation/rotation sensor. 0/1.
House-keeping charging-status input. 0/1.
Raw battery-voltage ADC reading, 10-bit (0-1023) -- ATmega2560's built-in ADC, no external converter on this input.
Raw an0_in..an3_in ADC readings, 10-bit each (0-1023).

Raw value of main.cpp's volatile timeStatistics accumulator (accumulated TCNT2 ticks). Send as-is, unaveraged -- pair with time_counter below to compute the same ratio the firmware's own status bar does.
Raw value of main.cpp's volatile timeCounter (number of ticks accumulated into time_statistics so far, resets at 100).

message.name: CAN_SIGNAL_CONFIG
message.description: Configure/start/stop a generated signal on one of the board's 2 CAN buses. One active signal per bus -- sending a new config for a bus_id replaces whatever was previously configured there. The board transmits exactly the given bytes on a schedule; no waveform math happens on-board. PC -> board, command.
message.field: Target CAN bus: 0 or 1.
CAN identifier (standard or extended, see extended_id).
0 = standard 11-bit ID, 1 = extended 29-bit ID.
Data length, 0-8 (classic CAN).
Frame payload bytes; only the first dlc bytes are used.
Repeat interval in ms. 0 = send once (one-shot).
Number of times to send. 0 = repeat until disabled.
1 = start/keep running, 0 = stop. Resend with 0 to stop a running generator.

message.name: RS485_SIGNAL_CONFIG
message.description: Configure/start/stop a generated signal on the board's RS-485 connection. One active signal at a time -- a new config replaces whatever was previously running. Raw byte transmission, no framing imposed (no protocol defined over this link yet). PC -> board, command.
message.field: Valid byte count in data, 0-32.
Raw payload bytes; only the first length bytes are used.
Repeat interval in ms. 0 = send once (one-shot).
Number of times to send. 0 = repeat until disabled.
1 = start/keep running, 0 = stop. Resend with 0 to stop a running generator.

message.name: PWM_CHANNEL_CONFIG
message.description:
Configure one of the board's 4 PWM channels. PC -> board, command. The board applies it to the timer registers immediately; there is no ack. Sending a new config for a channel replaces its previous one (last writer wins, including against the on-screen PWM tab, which drives the same registers).
One message shape covers both channel kinds (see IHM/lib/MultiOutput/src/PWM.h): * channels 0 and 1 are "simplex" -- a single output (OC3A / OC5A). Only out1_* is used; out2_* and out3_* are ignored. * channels 2 and 3 are "complex" -- three independent outputs A/B/C (OC1A/B/C, OC4A/B/C). out1_/out2_/out3_ map to A/B/C.
Same "not bit-packed across byte boundaries" convention as the other messages here -- each flag gets its own byte. 13 bytes, well under the 64-byte cap.
message.field: Target PWM channel, 0-3. Out-of-range configs are dropped by the board.
Frequency selector for the whole channel.
Raw ICRn TOP (timer period). Only read when f_selector == PWM_FREQUENCY_VARIABLE; ignored for every fixed selector.
Output A: 1 = drive the pin, 0 = disconnect it.
Output A: 0 = non-inverting (high from period start), 1 = inverting.
Output A duty cycle, 0-100. Scaled against the selector's resolution on-board.
Output B enable. Ignored for channels 0 and 1.
Output B edge polarity. Ignored for channels 0 and 1.
Output B duty cycle, 0-100. Ignored for channels 0 and 1.
Output C enable. Ignored for channels 0 and 1.
Output C edge polarity. Ignored for channels 0 and 1.
Output C duty cycle, 0-100. Ignored for channels 0 and 1.

message.name: IHM_RELAY_STATE
message.description: Periodic snapshot of all 8 relay outputs. Board -> PC, telemetry, read-only -- there is no PC -> board relay command yet (relays are only toggled locally, by the physical buttons or the on-screen Relay tab). Mirrors main.cpp's relayState[NUMBER_OF_RELAYS] the same way IHM_BOARD_STATE.buttons mirrors the button bitmap.
message.field: Bitmask, bit i = relay i (0-7), 1 = on.

message.name: IHM_SIMULATE_ENCODER
message.description: PC injects one simulated rotation step on the given encoder. The board applies it only if that encoder's real hardware read was idle (not_supported) on the same superloop pass -- real input always wins, no fight between the two sources. Consumed exactly once, mirroring the real encoder's own edge-triggered/consumed- on-read semantics (RotaryEncoder.h). No ack. PC -> board, command.
message.field: Target encoder, 0-2. Out-of-range is dropped by the board.
CW or CCW; NOT_SUPPORTED is a no-op.
